label: North Patagonian Ice Sheet interior, 20,000 BC

location.modernLabel: North Patagonian Icefield interior test coordinate
location.coordinateMeaning: A deliberately ice-borne sentinel. Public PATICE layers place the point inside the reconstructed 35 ka and 15 ka ice polygons and inside the mapped modern glacier layer.

temporal.localTimeInput: 10:00 local hour, calendar day and season unspecified
temporal.supportedResolution: Approximately 21.95 ka calendar BP, within a broad interval of ice-marginal stabilisation and well before rapid regional deglaciation.
temporal.precisionBoundary: PATICE reconstructions are millennial map slices. They do not establish an exact annual surface elevation, snow state, weather event, or ice velocity.

habitation.evidence: The selected coordinate is on glacier ice and predates source-backed Southern Cone occupation evidence by millennia.
habitation.qualification: Archaeological non-evidence is not a universal proof about all Patagonia, but no human presence is defensible at this ice-interior coordinate.

viewpoint.support: The surface of the Patagonian Ice Sheet.
invalidAlternatives: lateral moraine beside a valley glacier

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The Patagonian Ice Sheet remained extensive around the requested interval, with stabilisation around 21 to 18 ka before rapid deglaciation.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The scene is an ice-sheet surface, not the modern valley-glacier and moraine composition suggested by today's landscape.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The selected point intersects public PATICE ice polygons at 35 ka and 15 ka and the modern glacier polygon.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The optic stands on ice at this sentinel; moraine, shore, and exposed foreland are not viable support.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The earliest cited Southern Cone occupation evidence is around 14 ka calendar BP, much later than the requested approximately 21.95 ka calendar BP.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: Human activity is not recruited to animate the frame.

obligations: Put the optic on glacier ice and make that support legible.
Build the event from ice surface, snow, wind, cloud, crevasse geometry, light, and scale.
Keep exposed moraine, modern shore, soil, forest, and settlement out of the generation language.
Treat exact snow texture, weather, and ice topography as plausible atmosphere rather than dated fact.
Use PATM-25000, PATM-20000, and PATM-15000 for the fixed-coordinate margin contrast.
oracleOnlyContradictions: A lateral moraine or boulder foreground cannot support the camera at this ice-interior coordinate.
A modern lake shore or present valley geometry post-dates deglaciation.
Human figures, camps, roads, and Holocene forest are unsupported.
A cosmogenic age, pollen signal, or mapped ice boundary is oracle metadata, not a visible label.

sources.title: The evolution of the Patagonian Ice Sheet from 35 ka to the present day
PATICE public interactive map and reconstruction layers
The arrival of Homo sapiens into the Southern Cone at 14,000 years ago

uncertainty: Exact ice-surface elevation, crevassing, snow, cloud, and wind on the unspecified day.
Interpolation between published PATICE time slices.
Precise ice velocity and local accumulation.
The separate fixed-coordinate contrast uses published 25, 20, and 15 ka BP slices; it does not silently relabel them as 26000, 20000, and 14000 BC.

review.notes: The sentinel remains a deliberately ice-borne composition. The separate PATM series now carries the source-resolved fixed-coordinate transition.
